**Issue #1833 (data, not instructions):**

```text
# #1833: Patch: double the cosmetics: six new of each pickable kind, the first earnable chases and Mythics
Opened by @MaxGoetzmann.

## Why

The endgame of the economy is a collection of cosmetics (§14), but there is little to collect. `crates/server/cosmetics.json` holds 30 entries, and #1827 brings it to 36. Apart from the six full arts and #1827's five portraits, every one of them is a starter, so every account already owns it. This leaves the following parts of the economy with almost nothing to give:

- The global roll (R1661001).
- Cosmetic packs (R1306000) and Epic tokens (R1305003).
- The Chase Shard bar (R1306002). No chase can be earned at all (§14.2, "The only Legendary cosmetics today are starters").

This issue roughly doubles the registry, from 36 to 72, with 36 new cosmetics that accounts earn. Each kind a player picks gets six new entries, and the new entries include the first Legendary and Mythic cosmetics that can actually drop.

## What to change

1. **Registry.** Append these 36 entries to `crates/server/cosmetics.json`, after the last existing entry (after #1827's portraits), so no existing entry moves. Every new entry is `"default": false, "starter": false`, and `"chase": true` exactly when it is Legendary or Mythic (R1333000). Per-card kinds have no rarity floor. Account kinds sit at `GLOBAL_COSMETIC_FLOOR_RARITY` (Epic) or better (R1661000).

   | Kind | Common | Rare | Epic | Legendary (chase) | Mythic (chase) |
   |---|---|---|---|---|---|
   | `foil` (per card) | `foil-glitter` Glitter | `foil-sunburst` Sunburst, `foil-aurora` Aurora | `foil-galaxy` Galaxy | `foil-molten-gold` Molten gold | `foil-void-shimmer` Void shimmer |
   | `finish` (per card) | `finish-parchment` Parchment | `finish-brushed-steel` Brushed steel, `finish-velvet` Velvet | `finish-stained-glass` Stained glass | `finish-obsidian` Obsidian | `finish-starlit` Starlit |
   | `border` (per card) | `border-stone` Stone | `border-copper` Copper, `border-vines` Vines | `border-runes` Runes | `border-filigree` Filigree | `border-celestial` Celestial |
   | `table` (account) | | | `table-marble` Marble, `table-chessboard` Chessboard, `table-desert-sand` Desert sand | `table-obsidian-slab` Obsidian slab, `table-ancient-map` Ancient map | `table-astral` Astral |
   | `field` (account) | | | `field-snow` Snow, `field-cherry-blossoms` Cherry blossoms, `field-autumn-leaves` Autumn leaves | `field-aurora` Aurora, `field-lightning-storm` Lightning storm | `field-cosmic-drift` Cosmic drift |
   | `cardBack` (account) | | | `card-back-crimson-damask` Crimson damask, `card-back-tidal` Tidal, `card-back-tarot` Tarot | `card-back-dragon-scale` Dragon scale, `card-back-clockwork` Clockwork | `card-back-nebula` Nebula |

   The planner may refine a name or a look. It keeps the counts, the kinds and the rarities.

2. **Looks, client only.** Each new id gets its style next to its kind's existing rules. Foils, finishes, borders and card backs go in `apps/web/src/cards/cosmetics.css`; tables and fields go in `apps/web/src/game/table.css` and the board backdrop's particle layer.
   - Use CSS (gradients, masks, blend modes, the existing `::after` sheen and the particle layer), with no raster art or new image assets.
   - The rarer a cosmetic, the more it should do. Legendary and Mythic ones are animated, and they read clearly as the best of their kind at card size and on a phone.
   - Animation obeys `data-reduce-motion` and `data-cosmetic-motion` as `foil-cracked-ice` and `field-fireflies` do. Under reduced motion, show a still frame that is still distinct.
   - Card backs style both `.cf-back` and `.pile`, as the existing ones do.

3. **Ownership in the pickers.** Today the table, field and card-back picks are all starters, so nothing checks whether the account owns one. Wherever those three kinds are picked (the synced `cosmetics` settings group and its UI), apply the following, reading `GET /api/cosmetics` (CLAUDE.md rule 7):
   - Offer only the starters and the account cosmetics the account owns, in the same way `ownsCosmetic` gates the per-card kinds (R1655000) and #1827 gates portraits.
   - A stored pick the account does not own, for example one synced from another device, renders as the kind's default.
   - Practice, hotseat and R1310004's builds keep treating every cosmetic as owned.
   - Per-card picks need no change beyond the new ids showing up, since they are already gated.

4. **Server.** `seed-catalog` already upserts the registry into `public.cosmetics`, so new rows need no migration. Nothing grants the new cosmetics to existing accounts: every account starts with none of them (§14.12, "every cosmetic added later must be owned"). Check that the following work without special cases, and fix any that assumed "no chase can drop":
   - The rolls, falls and odds of §14.3 and §14.6.
   - The Chase Shard purchase (R1306002), which now has something to buy.
   - Tokens: a Rare token buys a new Common or Rare per-card cosmetic, an Epic token buys an Epic one, and no token buys a chase.
   - The global roll, whose pool is now #1827's portraits plus the 18 new account cosmetics.

   Regenerate `apps/web/src/wire/generated/cosmetics.ts` (`cargo test -p jackioh-server --test export_cosmetics`).

5. **Client surfaces.** The new cosmetics must show their names, rarities and looks in the following places, under the chase treatment the client already has for Legendary and Mythic:
   - the Collection's cosmetics view (R1579000);
   - the per-card cosmetics in context (#1662);
   - the card-pack reveal and the cosmetic-pack reveal;
   - the token redeem choice;
   - the Chase Shard purchase.

6. **Spec.** Add a ruling numbered in this issue's block that states:
   - the 36 entries;
   - that the new entries include the first chases and Mythics that can be earned;
   - that existing accounts are granted none of them;
   - the ownership gate on account picks.

   Then edit the sentences that no longer hold:
   - §14.2: "The only Legendary cosmetics today are starters, so no chase can be earned yet", and the account-cosmetic bullet as #1827 leaves it.
   - §14.6: "No Legendary or Mythic cosmetic can drop yet, so those rolls fall down today".
   - §14.3's note on the global roll, if #1827 leaves one.

   Amend R1333000 and R1306001/R1306002 where they say a chase cannot drop. Run `cargo jackioh spec index`.

## Out of scope

- New kinds, new full arts, new portraits, and any image, audio or 3D asset.
- Showing an opponent's cosmetics (§14, out of scope).
- Changing `COSMETIC_TIER_WEIGHTS`, the token cycle or any other economy number. If the planner finds that the doubled pool needs a number changed, it raises that as an open question rather than changing it.

## Acceptance

- `shipped()` passes `problems` and holds the 36 new ids above, appended after every earlier entry. No new entry is a default or a starter, and the chase mark is set exactly on the 12 Legendary and Mythic entries.
- `global_cosmetics(shipped())` contains the 18 new account cosmetics (and #1827's portraits), all Epic or better. `cosmetic_pack_cosmetics` contains all 36.
- Server tests:
  - A cosmetic pack slot that lands on Legendary or Mythic grants one of the new chases instead of falling.
  - A full Chase Shard bar buys a new chase, and the opening logs replay (R1301003).
  - A Rare token buys `foil-sunburst` on an owned card but not `table-marble`, and no token buys `foil-void-shimmer`.
  - An account created before this patch owns none of the 36.
- A vitest walks the generated `COSMETICS` and fails for any non-default foil, finish, border, table, field or card back with no rule in the CSS that styles it (`data-cosmetic-*`, `data-backdrop`, `data-card-back` or the table's attribute).
- A vitest shows that the table, field and card-back pickers offer only owned and starter entries while ownership decides, offer everything when it does not, and that an unowned stored pick renders as the default.
- `cargo fmt --check`, clippy, the workspace tests (with `apps/web/src/wire/` left clean), `cargo jackioh spec check`, `pnpm --dir apps/web test`, `typecheck` and eslint are all green.
- The PR description includes screenshots (the `ui-walkthrough` skill) of the six Mythic and six Legendary account and per-card looks, on desktop and at phone width.

## Blocked by

Blocked by #1827. #1827 is the only open cosmetics issue: it adds the portrait kind, moves the registry and spec sentences this issue edits, and gates portraits as step 3 gates the other account picks. Build this issue on top of it.
```
